purpose: Protect existing installations and finish the requested browser acceptance fixes before broader introduction
status: Implemented and validated locally; no commit, publication or household deployment

environment.notification_delivery: Isolated synthetic services and captured requests only

changes: Replace the earlier default-settings reset with zero-delay conversion of supported older named-notification settings; preserve existing choices and do not restore deleted defaults.
Reject pre-collection delivery envelopes before setup mutates settings or starts runtime; actual published older state reproduced alert replay without this guard.
Persist converted settings only after actual public engine and policy restoration and evaluation succeed, before state saving or notification requests.

Keep narrow Monitoring headings and Back visible under the actual wrapped header; use overflow clipping without an intermediate scroll container, retain heading focus through evidence loading and wrap enlarged names and header controls.
Hide retained availability badges when complete current evidence contains only missing or restored reports; retain independently qualified conditions and live unavailable findings.
Restore the selected Monitoring source after nested policy and native Home Assistant navigation.
Update stale entity-availability, combined-device selection, timing and frontend-upgrade assertions, and add real-HA coverage for previously untested provider, badge and navigation paths.
Correct onboarding defaults and document preserving upgrades and visible unsupported-state failures.

upgrade_protection.historical_state: Synthetic presented and queued snapshots generated by the actual published earlier releases are rejected with original data, options and store unchanged and zero notification requests.
upgrade_protection.supported_conversion: Absent saved state or a compatible current delivery envelope; add collection delay 0 and apply the existing validated device-policy conversion without replacing saved preferences.
upgrade_protection.invalid_restore: Corrupt engine and policy restore cases preserve original configuration and store across explicit refresh, timer advance, unload and another setup; no state writes or sends.
upgrade_protection.current_installations: Both storage locations, sending on/off, edited and deleted defaults, disabled choices, selectors/exclusions, named and Custom assignments, destinations, history, acknowledgments, pauses and stable outbox replay are covered.
upgrade_protection.startup: Cold start performs no conversion write before Home Assistant starts; successful conversion does not trigger recursive reload and the next explicit reload is unchanged.

validation.rendered_narrow_matrix: 320px and 390px, normal and doubled text, pointer and keyboard; eight real-HA combinations plus fixture checks, including title/Back geometry, hit testing, focus return and unchanged settings.

reconnect.owner: Native Home Assistant persistent-notification cleanup reused an old subscription ID on the new socket; the ID belonged to frontend/get_translations in the reproduced run.
reconnect.homeostatic_checks: All eight checks pass: same connection, one replacement subscription, invalidated disconnected baseline, read-only stale editor, retained draft/DOM/focus/selection, fresh live update, unchanged saved settings and zero saves.
reconnect.limit: The correction was present on upstream master; no matched released HA frontend upgrade was validated. Homeostatic does not patch the shared HA connection.

evidence_accounting.preserved_full_run_failure: Both full runs retain the stale delivery-picker current-element assertion after the frontend version bump. Only the fixture HTML and scenario identities were corrected; the complete fixture matrix was then rerun for both viewports.
evidence_accounting.layer_selection: Real-HA results come from the complete original final runs; fixture results come from the complete corrected fixture-only runs. All four used identical production component bytes. Reports with different fixture hashes were not merged, and no earlier failure was erased.
evidence_accounting.fixture_coverage_note: workspace.html passes its own checks but declares no inventory receipt; it contributes no claimed inventory coverage. The first five fixture-only gaps are covered by the real-HA runs.
evidence_accounting.environment_retries: Preserved a quick-check attempt using unsupported Node18 and fixture launch attempts missing the Linux audio library. Prepared Node24 and the existing browser runtime resolved these without product edits.

limits: The whole browser suite is not clean: the attributed native Home Assistant reconnect failure remains in both real-HA reports.
Real notification-provider receipt, a fresh human onboarding walkthrough, release CI and packaged clean-install verification are not established by these isolated runs.
Older pre-collection delivery state is deliberately blocked; this change does not provide an engine-state migration for it.
No household installation or saved household setting was changed, and no live notification was requested.
The corrections remain uncommitted, unreleased and undeployed; the current public release does not yet contain these protections.
